html:
Saylan is an old Arabic and Persian name for Sri Lanka. On the 1530 and 1600 maps it marks the island in the century when the Portuguese arrived and its kingdoms fought for survival.

In 1505 the island was divided. The Kingdom of Kotte near Colombo was the leading power, the Jaffna Kingdom held the Tamil north, and Kandy held the central hills. Ships of Portugal came for cinnamon and built a fort at Colombo.

In 1521 Kotte split three ways. From one piece, the Kingdom of Sitawaka grew strong under Mayadunne and his son Rajasinghe I, who besieged Portuguese Colombo in 1587 and 1588. Kotte's own king, Dharmapala, became a Catholic and left his kingdom to Portugal, which took it over in 1597. Kandy resisted and crushed a Portuguese army at the Battle of Danture in 1594. The island's later story is on the page Ceylon.
